newsitem.title: USA: California child gets cocaine-laced Halloween treat.
newsitem.headline: California child gets cocaine-laced Halloween treat.

text.p: A 7-year-old boy was treated at a hospital after apparently being given a cocaine-laced treat on Halloween, police said on Friday.
Ferdinan Siquig was out with family and friends in San Jose on Thursday night when he collapsed after eating candy and cookies he was given while "trick-or-treating."
Children, typically in costume, go door-to-door for candy and other treats on Halloween.

Siquig was taken to a local hospital where urine analysis revealed traces of cocaine in his system. He was released early on Friday and was in good condition, San Jose police spokesman Louis Quezada said.
Quezada said the poisoning appeared to be an isolated incident and police were going door-to-door in the neighbourhood as they investigated.
He said police had no suspects yet. If found, the suspect could be charged with attempted murder. "To us it's atrocious that someone would do something like this," he said.

San Jose police advised parents and school officials to check all candy and pastry thoroughly before allowing chidren to eat anything that was given to them on Halloween and to throw away items that were not pre-packaged.
